characteristics: T-64BM Bulat adds Ukrainian Nozh ERA and improved optics
Strength: Most numerous pre-war Ukrainian MBT; crews highly experienced on the type; fast autoloader
Limitation: Fleet is irreplaceable — no foreign source for more T-64s once lost, unlike T-72/T-80 which allies also operate; underpowered engine for added ERA weight
Estimated quantity available: ~250-300 T-64BV/BM estimated remaining as of early 2023 reporting; further attrition since
employment_notes: Ukraine went to war with ~800 T-64s; roughly half lost within the first year; increasingly used as static/indirect fire platforms as the fleet depletes, since losses can't be replaced from abroad
contrast_vs_traditional: Cold War Soviet armor doctrine massed T-64s in echelon for a breakthrough, with losses expected but absorbed by numbers. Ukraine is fighting with the same airframes that doctrine assumed would be replaced from a Soviet-scale production line that no longer exists, so each Bulat upgrade is a bet on keeping a 1960s-era hull survivable against a threat — top-attack FPVs — its designers never modeled, rather than a step toward a successor design.
